problems.statement: The group-wide 19-minute ticket time is not a new kitchen inefficiency: it is a deliberate, board-approved cost of the October 2024 'Made Here' scratch menu, stable at about 17-18 minutes for 21 months, and it comes with higher food quality, check, same-store sales and repeat visits.

The 12-minute benchmark is not comparable because the panel is limited to chains that assemble 60% or more of their menu from pre-prepared or frozen components and excludes scratch kitchens, and its check size is lower.

The 19.1-minute group average is inflated by Riverside alone. The other eight locations average 17.6 minutes, unchanged from their Jan-Jul 2026 mean, so the group has no new deterioration outside Riverside.

Riverside's ticket-time spike, falling reviews and rising comps stem from a staffing gap at the saute/pasta station that has gone unfilled since Delgado left on 2026-08-08. The gap is worst on Friday and Saturday dinners, with a cross-training prep cook covering the station, and the transfer requests were deferred by group operations.
Riverside's problem is caused by its general manager's poor leadership, so replacing him would fix it.
The scratch-cooking menu itself drives Riverside's deterioration, so par-cooked components would fix it.
Par-cooked and frozen components would deliver the projected 12.5-minute ticket time and 6% labor savings at no cost to the guest experience.
Ticket time is a guest-experience problem across the group, driven by speed of service.
Tying GM bonuses to a 12-minute ticket time would improve kitchen performance.

The June 2026 Sunday hour cut contributed to Delgado's resignation, but his reason for leaving is unresolved: his own account is a spouse's job move and a line cook attributes it to the cut. The cut was applied to all four line cooks, followed a 21% Sunday cover drop and complied with group operations' labor standard.

actions.action: Fill the Riverside saute/pasta vacancy now: approve a transfer cook or temporary cover, and expedite hiring, so that Friday and Saturday dinners have a full line.
actions.rationale: This addresses the mechanism behind 71% of the rise in Riverside's ticket time. It is cheap and reversible, and its benefit does not depend on any unconfirmed explanation.

actions.action: Lift the 'pending ownership staffing review' deferral on transfer and hiring requests, and set a rapid decision path for urgent line vacancies.
actions.rationale: Group operations' own deferrals prolonged the gap, so fixing the process addresses part of the cause.

actions.action: Review Riverside labor scheduling against forecast covers, including Friday and Saturday dinner coverage, and consider restoring cuts on peak days.
actions.rationale: The cuts followed the bridge closure and the labor standard, but the unfilled position on peak nights is now costing sales, reviews and comps.

actions.action: Re-set the ticket-time target against the group's own scratch-menu baseline of about 17.5 minutes, with a Riverside recovery target of about 18 minutes, and monitor against the 19-minute board ceiling.
actions.rationale: The benchmark is not comparable, whereas the board's own ceiling and the 21-month baseline are.

actions.action: Roll out par-cooked and frozen components across all nine kitchens.
actions.rationale: The trial showed a quality drop, and the 1.9-minute gain is less than half the benchmark gap. The group's food-quality scores, check size, same-store sales and repeat visits rest on the scratch positioning, and the Riverside problem is staffing, so the change would not fix it.

actions.action: Write a 12-minute ticket-time target into every GM's bonus from Q1 2027.
actions.rationale: The target is unachievable under the current menu, and the 2023 audit showed ticket-time bonuses led to KDS bumping with no gain in guest scores.
The evidence points to staffing and deferred transfers, with group operations contributing. The GM's role in Delgado's departure is disputed, and removing him would not fill the vacant station.

actions.action: Interview Delgado, if he is reachable, and review the GM's scheduling decisions as part of the Riverside review.
actions.rationale: This would settle whether leadership is a separate contributor, at low cost.

actions.action: If ownership wants faster ticket times, run a board-level decision on the menu trade-off, using the group's own station time study, with a quality and repeat-visit analysis.
actions.rationale: The repeat-visit measurement changed in October 2024 and is not reconciled, so the scratch menu's commercial value should be confirmed before any strategic change.

nextEvidence: Exit interview or direct contact with Marcus Delgado, plus any written Sunday-hours communications, to settle why he left and whether the GM's scheduling contributed.
Riverside's KDS station timings and ticket times for the first weeks after a vacancy is filled, to confirm that the station gap is the cause and that times recover to about 18 minutes.
A reconciled repeat-visit and revenue analysis by location, covering the scratch-menu effect and any cost of lower speed of service, to quantify the commercial value of the Made Here positioning.
output.summary: The 19-minute group average is not a new inefficiency. It reflects the board-approved 2024 scratch menu, which raised ticket time to about 17.5 minutes and has held there for 21 months, alongside higher food scores, check, sales and repeat visits. The 12-minute benchmark excludes scratch kitchens, so it is not comparable. Eight locations average 17.6 minutes, and Riverside alone lifts the average. Riverside's decline comes from an unfilled saute/pasta vacancy, made worse by deferred transfer requests, not from the menu. Fill the vacancy now. Do not go to par-cooked food, a 12-minute GM bonus (gaming risk) or a leadership change on this evidence.
